## Overview

The initial gene catalogue contained prokaryotic ORFs. To ensure a reliable
assessment of the metabolic potential of microbial eukaryotes in the water column,
the catalogue was curated through a multi-step process:

1. **Taxonomic Assignment** — three parallel MMseqs2 searches against eukaryotic and
   mixed reference databases.
2. **Tax ID Score Filtering** — retention of ORFs with hits in all three databases,
   scored by a weighted combination of query coverage and percent identity.
3. **MATOU Validation** — cross-validation against the Marine Atlas of Tara Oceans
   Unigenes eukaryotic reference.
4. **Consensus Taxonomy** — derivation of the lowest common taxonomic ancestor for
   each retained gene.

### Dependencies

```{r dependencies}
library(taxize)       # NCBI lineage retrieval
library(data.table)   # fast in-memory operations
library(dplyr)        # data manipulation
library(stringr)      # string operations
```

---

## Step 1 — Taxonomic Assignment

Three parallel taxonomic assignments were performed using the `easy-taxonomy` module
from MMseqs2 (Steinegger & Söding, 2017) against three reference databases:

| Database | Content | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| **EukProt** | Eukaryotic sequences only | Richter et al., 2020 |
| **MarFERReT v1.1.1** | Eukaryotic sequences only | Groussman et al., 2023 |
| **MMETSP\_Uniclust90** | Eukaryotic + prokaryotic sequences | Keeling et al., 2014; Mirdita et al., 2017 |

The MMETSP\_Uniclust90 database was assembled from the Marine Microbial Eukaryote
Transcriptome Sequencing Project (MMETSP) and Uniclust90, and is the only database
that includes prokaryotic references — allowing detection of potential prokaryotic
contamination.

LCA mode 4 was used (`--lca-mode 4`), which applies a top-hit-based LCA to produce
conservative taxonomic assignments.

Each run was submitted as an independent HPC job. The commands below can be
adapted to any SLURM-based cluster by updating the database paths and output
directories.

### 1a — EukProt

```{bash step1-eukprot}
module load mmseqs2/13-45111

QUERY=analyses/malaspina_catalogue_fasta/EukMPGC_95id_m250bp.faa
DB=/path/to/EukProt.tax/sequenceDB
OUTDIR=analyses/taxonomy_EukProt
OUTPUT=${OUTDIR}/taxonomyResults_EukProt

mkdir -p ${OUTDIR}

mmseqs easy-taxonomy \
  ${QUERY} ${DB} ${OUTPUT} ${OUTDIR}/tmp \
  --lca-mode 4 \
  --format-output "query,target,pident,alnlen,mismatch,gapopen,qstart,qend,tstart,tend,evalue,bits,qlen,tlen,taxid,taxname,taxlineage" \
  --threads 12
```

### 1b — MarFERReT

```{bash step1-marferret}
module load mmseqs2/13-45111

QUERY=analyses/malaspina_catalogue_fasta/EukMPGC_95id_m250bp.faa
DB=/path/to/MarFERReT/v1.1.1/mmseqs2/MarFERReTDB
OUTDIR=analyses/taxonomy_MarFERReT
OUTPUT=${OUTDIR}/taxonomyResults_MarFERReT

mkdir -p ${OUTDIR}

mmseqs easy-taxonomy \
  ${QUERY} ${DB} ${OUTPUT} ${OUTDIR}/tmp \
  --lca-mode 4 \
  --format-output "query,target,pident,alnlen,mismatch,gapopen,qstart,qend,tstart,tend,evalue,bits,qlen,tlen,taxid,taxname,taxlineage" \
  --threads 12
```

### 1c — MMETSP\_Uniclust90

```{bash step1-mmetsp}
module load mmseqs2/13-45111

QUERY=analyses/malaspina_catalogue_fasta/EukMPGC_95id_m250bp.faa
DB=/path/to/MMETSP_zenodo_3247846_uniclust90_2018_08_seed_valid_taxids
OUTDIR=analyses/taxonomy_MMETSP_Uni90
OUTPUT=${OUTDIR}/taxonomyResults_MMETSP_Uni90

mkdir -p ${OUTDIR}

mmseqs easy-taxonomy \
  ${QUERY} ${DB} ${OUTPUT} ${OUTDIR}/tmp \
  --lca-mode 4 \
  --format-output "query,target,pident,alnlen,mismatch,gapopen,qstart,qend,tstart,tend,evalue,bits,qlen,tlen,taxid,taxname,taxlineage" \
  --threads 12
```

---

## Step 2 — Tax ID Score Comparison

Only ORFs with hits in **all three databases** were retained for downstream curation
(n = 17,348,923). This ensures that every retained ORF can be compared across
databases and reliably assigned to eukaryotes.

For each ORF, the best taxonomic hit was selected using the **Tax ID score**, defined
as a weighted sum of query coverage and percent identity:

$$\text{Tax ID score} = 0.6 \times \text{query coverage} + 0.4 \times \text{pident}$$

Query coverage (alignment length / query length, capped at 100) was weighted more
heavily than percent identity because a hit spanning a larger proportion of the query
provides a more reliable basis for taxonomic assignment than a short, highly similar
alignment — which may reflect conserved domains shared across distantly related taxa.

Only **eukaryotic hits** (Domain = Eukaryota) with **e-value < 1e-5** and the
**highest Tax ID score** per ORF were retained, yielding **8,139,291 putative
eukaryotic ORFs**.

### 2.1 — Load MMseqs2 top-hit alignment files

```{r load-tophits}
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

# Read raw MMseqs2 top-hit alignment tables (no header — columns as per
# --format-output string used in Step 1)
eukprot_tophit   <- fread("analyses/taxonomy_EukProt/taxonomyResults_EukProt_tophit_aln")
marferret_tophit <- fread("analyses/taxonomy_MarFERReT/taxonomyResults_MarFERReT_tophit_aln")
mmetsp_tophit    <- fread("analyses/taxonomy_MMETSP_Uni90/taxonomyResults_MMETSP_Uni90_tophit_aln")

# Save as RDS for fast reload
saveRDS(eukprot_tophit,   "eukprot_tophit_alignment.RDS")
saveRDS(marferret_tophit, "marferret_tophit_alignment.RDS")
saveRDS(mmetsp_tophit,    "mmetsp_uni90_tophit_alignment.RDS")
```

### 2.2 — Identify genes with hits in all three databases

```{r shared-genes}
eukprot_tophit   <- readRDS("eukprot_tophit_alignment.RDS")
marferret_tophit <- readRDS("marferret_tophit_alignment.RDS")
mmetsp_tophit    <- readRDS("mmetsp_uni90_tophit_alignment.RDS")

# Retain only ORFs present in all three search results (n = 17,348,923)
shared_genes <- base::intersect(
  base::intersect(eukprot_tophit$V1, marferret_tophit$V1),
  mmetsp_tophit$V1
)

saveRDS(shared_genes, "genes_shared_all_databases.RDS")
```

### 2.3 — Compute Tax ID score and select best eukaryotic hit

```{r taxid-score}
shared_genes <- readRDS("genes_shared_all_databases.RDS")

# Filter each database to shared genes and label the source
eukprot_tophit <- readRDS("eukprot_tophit_alignment.RDS") %>%
  filter(V1 %in% shared_genes) %>%
  mutate(taxdb = "eukprot")

marferret_tophit <- readRDS("marferret_tophit_alignment.RDS") %>%
  filter(V1 %in% shared_genes) %>%
  mutate(taxdb = "marferret")

mmetsp_tophit <- readRDS("mmetsp_uni90_tophit_alignment.RDS") %>%
  filter(V1 %in% shared_genes) %>%
  mutate(taxdb = "mmetsp_uni90")

# Combine all three into one table and assign column names
all_hits <- rbind(eukprot_tophit, marferret_tophit, mmetsp_tophit)

colnames(all_hits) <- c(
  "query", "target", "pident", "alnlen", "mismatch", "gapopen",
  "qstart", "qend", "tstart", "tend", "evalue",
  "bits", "qlen", "tlen", "taxid", "taxname", "taxlineage", "taxdb"
)

# Compute Tax ID score and retain best eukaryotic hit per ORF
best_eukaryotic_hits <- all_hits %>%
  mutate(domain = str_extract(taxlineage, "(?<=d_)[^;]+")) %>%
  mutate(domain = ifelse(is.na(domain), "unclassified", domain)) %>%
  filter(evalue < 1e-5) %>%                              # significance threshold
  mutate(q_cov = (alnlen / qlen) * 100) %>%
  mutate(q_cov = ifelse(q_cov > 100, 100, q_cov)) %>%   # cap at 100
  mutate(tax_id_score = (q_cov * 0.6) + (pident * 0.4)) %>%
  group_by(query) %>%
  slice_max(tax_id_score) %>%
  ungroup()

saveRDS(best_eukaryotic_hits, "best_taxid_score_hits.RDS")

# Subset to eukaryotic domain only
mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits <- best_eukaryotic_hits %>%
  filter(grepl("Eukaryot", domain))   # n = 8,139,291

saveRDS(mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits, "mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits.RDS")

eukaryotic_gene_ids <- unique(mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits$query)
saveRDS(eukaryotic_gene_ids, "eukaryotic_gene_ids.RDS")
```

---

## Step 3 — MATOU Validation

The 8,139,291 putative eukaryotic ORFs were cross-validated against the Marine Atlas
of Tara Oceans Unigenes (MATOU) reference protein database (Carradec et al., 2018),
derived from eukaryotic metatranscriptomics data, using the MMseqs2 `search` tool.
Only the single best hit per query (`--max-seqs 1`) was retrieved. Hits with
**e-value < 1e−5** were retained, yielding **7,714,686 eukaryotic ORFs**.

### 3.1 — MMseqs2 search against MATOU

**Inputs:**
- `eukaryotic_gene_catalogue.fasta` — putative eukaryotic ORF sequences (Step 2 output)
- `matou_reference_proteins.faa` — MATOU reference protein sequences

**Output:** `matou_search_results.m8` — best-hit alignment table in BLAST tabular format.

```{bash step3-matou}
module load mmseqs2/13-45111

# Build MMseqs2 databases from FASTA files
mmseqs createdb eukaryotic_gene_catalogue.fasta queryDB
mmseqs createdb matou_reference_proteins.faa    targetDB

mkdir -p tmp
mkdir -p MATOU_validation

# Search: --max-seqs 1 retains only the single best hit per query
mmseqs search queryDB targetDB resultDB tmp --max-seqs 1 --threads 12

# Convert to BLAST tabular format (m8)
mmseqs convertalis queryDB targetDB resultDB \
  MATOU_validation/matou_search_results.m8 --threads 12
```

### 3.2 — Filter hits and extract verified gene list

```{r step3-filter}
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)

matou_hits <- fread(
  "MATOU_validation/matou_search_results.m8",
  col.names = c("gene_id", "target", "pident", "alnlen",
                "mismatch", "gapopen", "qstart", "qend",
                "tstart", "tend", "evalue", "bitscore")
)

saveRDS(matou_hits, "matou_search_results.RDS")

# Retain only hits with e-value < 1e-5
verified_hits <- matou_hits %>%
  filter(evalue < 1e-5)

verified_gene_catalogue <- unique(verified_hits$gene_id)  # n = 7,714,686

saveRDS(verified_gene_catalogue, "verified_gene_catalogue.RDS")
```

---

## Step 4 — Consensus Taxonomy Assignment

Each verified gene may receive hits against multiple organisms during MMseqs2 search,
resulting in a set of NCBI Taxonomy IDs rather than a single taxonomic assignment.
To derive a robust and conservative taxonomic label for each gene, we compute a
**lowest-common-ancestor (LCA)-style consensus**: the most specific NCBI taxon shared
by the largest number of hits. If no consensus is found beyond the domain level, only
the domain-level assignment is retained.

### 4.1 — Retrieve NCBI Taxonomic Lineages

Full NCBI lineages are retrieved using `taxize::classification()` with the `"ncbi"`
database — consistent with the taxonomy used by MMseqs2. The result is flattened
into a single data frame (one row per rank per taxid) and saved.

**Input:**  `mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits.RDS`
**Output:** `ncbi_taxonomic_lineages.RDS` — columns: `name`, `rank`, `id`, `query`
(where `query` is the queried taxid).

```{r retrieve-lineages}
library(taxize)

mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits <- readRDS("mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits.RDS")

ncbi_lineages_raw <- taxize::classification(
  unique(mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits$taxid),
  db = "ncbi"
)

# Flatten list → data frame
ncbi_lineages_df <- rbind(ncbi_lineages_raw)

saveRDS(ncbi_lineages_df, "ncbi_taxonomic_lineages.RDS")
```

### 4.2 — Compute Consensus Taxonomy per Gene

For each gene in the verified catalogue, `extract_consensus_taxonomy` identifies
the deepest taxonomic node supported by the majority of its hits and trims the
full lineage path to stop at that consensus point.

**Inputs:**
- `mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits.RDS`
- `verified_gene_catalogue.RDS` — gene IDs passing all quality filters (Step 3)
- `ncbi_taxonomic_lineages.RDS`

**Output:** `gene_consensus_taxonomy.RDS` — columns: `gene_id`, `taxid`,
`taxon_name`, `taxpath`.

```{r load-consensus-inputs}
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)

mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits <- readRDS("mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits.RDS")
verified_genes          <- readRDS("verified_gene_catalogue.RDS")
ncbi_lineages_df        <- readRDS("ncbi_taxonomic_lineages.RDS")

setDT(mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits)
setDT(ncbi_lineages_df)

hits_verified <- mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits %>%
  filter(query %in% verified_genes)
```

```{r consensus-function}
#' Consensus taxonomic assignment for a single gene.
#'
#' Algorithm:
#'   1. Collect all NCBI taxids from the gene's MMseqs2 hits.
#'   2. Retrieve the full ranked lineage (root → leaf) for each taxid.
#'   3. Score each taxon by (a) how many taxids share it and
#'      (b) how deep it sits in the tree. The winner is the most
#'      frequent taxon; depth breaks ties toward the more specific node.
#'   4. Trim the representative lineage string to end at the consensus taxon.
#'
#' @param gene_id  Character. A gene identifier present in `hits_verified$query`.
#' @return A one-row data frame: gene_id, taxid, taxon_name, taxpath.

extract_consensus_taxonomy <- function(gene_id) {

  # 1. Taxids assigned to this gene across all MMseqs2 hits
  gene_hits  <- hits_verified[which(hits_verified$query == gene_id), ]
  hit_taxids <- unique(gene_hits$taxid)

  # 2. Full NCBI lineages for those taxids (root → leaf order preserved)
  gene_lineages <- ncbi_lineages_df %>%
    filter(query %in% hit_taxids) %>%
    distinct()

  # 3. Consensus node:
  #    num    = depth rank within each taxid's lineage (1 = root)
  #    n_hits = number of taxids that share this taxon name
  consensus_node <- gene_lineages %>%
    mutate(num = row_number(), .by = "query") %>%
    add_count(name, name = "n_hits") %>%
    filter(n_hits == max(n_hits)) %>%   # most shared taxon(s)
    filter(num  == max(num))  %>%       # deepest among ties
    distinct()

  # 4. Build and trim the taxonomic path.
  #    Lineages of all taxids sharing the consensus node are concatenated;
  #    the first occurrence of the consensus name in the string always falls
  #    within the first lineage at the correct depth position.
  lineage_string <- gene_lineages %>%
    filter(query %in% consensus_node$query) %>%
    summarise(taxpath = paste(name, collapse = ";")) %>%
    pull(taxpath)

  split_path    <- unlist(strsplit(lineage_string, ";"))
  consensus_pos <- which(split_path == unique(consensus_node$name))[1]
  trimmed_path  <- paste(split_path[1:consensus_pos], collapse = ";")

  data.frame(
    gene_id    = gene_id,
    taxid      = unique(consensus_node$id),
    taxon_name = unique(consensus_node$name),
    taxpath    = trimmed_path
  )
}
```

```{r run-consensus}
consensus_list <- lapply(verified_genes, extract_consensus_taxonomy)

gene_consensus_taxonomy <- do.call(rbind, consensus_list)

saveRDS(gene_consensus_taxonomy, "gene_consensus_taxonomy.RDS")
```

## File Summary

| File | Step | Role |
|------|------|------|
| `EukMPGC_95id_m250bp.faa` | 1 | Input — gene catalogue protein sequences |
| `eukprot_tophit_alignment.RDS` | 2 | MMseqs2 EukProt top-hit alignment table |
| `marferret_tophit_alignment.RDS` | 2 | MMseqs2 MarFERReT top-hit alignment table |
| `mmetsp_uni90_tophit_alignment.RDS` | 2 | MMseqs2 MMETSP\_Uni90 top-hit alignment table |
| `genes_shared_all_databases.RDS` | 2 | Gene IDs with hits in all three databases (n = 17,348,923) |
| `best_taxid_score_hits.RDS` | 2 | Best hit per ORF ranked by Tax ID score |
| `mmseqs2_eukaryotic_hits.RDS` | 2 | Eukaryotic hits only (n = 8,139,291) |
| `eukaryotic_gene_ids.RDS` | 2 | Vector of eukaryotic ORF identifiers |
| `eukaryotic_gene_catalogue.fasta` | 3 | Input — putative eukaryotic ORF sequences |
| `matou_reference_proteins.faa` | 3 | Input — MATOU reference protein database |
| `matou_search_results.RDS` | 3 | MMseqs2 search results against MATOU |
| `verified_gene_catalogue.RDS` | 3 | ORFs validated against MATOU (n = 7,714,686) |
| `ncbi_taxonomic_lineages.RDS` | 4 | Full NCBI lineages per taxid (taxize output) |
| `gene_consensus_taxonomy.RDS` | 4 | **Final output** — consensus taxonomy per gene |

## Data Availability

The data files accompanying this pipeline — including the curated gene catalogue
(FASTA), consensus taxonomy table, ORF and KO count tables, and the KO–ORF key —
are deposited on Zenodo: [https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23557900](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23557900)
